sign_test_power.note: At n=16, sign test achieves >80% power for effects where >75% of events show suppression

minimum_detectable_effects.interpretation: n=16 can detect large effects (d>0.75) with 80% power; the observed RR=0.32 implies a very large effect

accident_n_needed_alpha0.05.note: Current n=29 gives P=0.067; need ~2 events for P<0.05

accident_n_needed_alpha0.01.note: Current n=29 gives P=0.067; need ~3 events for P<0.01

bayesian_perspective.interpretation: BF>100 is "decisive evidence" (Jeffreys); BF>10 is "strong evidence"
bayesian_perspective.note: Bayesian analysis converges across all reasonable priors, unlike frequentist tests that depend on n

specification_curve_strength.interpretation: 100% directional consistency across 180 specifications is astronomically unlikely under the null

precedent_small_n_studies.note: n=16 is typical for SSW event studies; the field accepts this sample size when effects are large and consistent
